{{Quote|Now Clan Varad has broken with the Mandalorian leadership and declared ''<nowiki>'</nowiki>akaan'gaan<nowiki>'</nowiki>''&mdash;the search for battle.|Darth Malgus|<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|[INTRO] Flashpoint: Mandalorian Raiders|Vaiken Spacedock}}</ref>}}
'''''Akaan'gaan''''' was a concept in ancient [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture. When translated from the Mandalorian [[Language/Legends|language]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], the term possessed the colloquial meaning of "the search for battle." Once declared, ''akaan'gaan'' denoted an individual or group's intent to seek open conflict wherever they may find it.<ref name="TOR" />

During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], the Mandalorian warrior [[Mavrix Varad]] led his clan to break away from the Empire with whom the Mandalorian people had been aligned. Declaring ''akaan'gaan'', [[Clan Varad]] stole a Republic [[Valor-class cruiser|''Valor''-class cruiser]] known as the ''[[Allusis]]'', and assaulted a number of Republic and Imperial targets<ref name="TOR" /> before they were finally [[Battle for the Allusis|neutralized]]<ref name="TOR:MR">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|Mandalorian Raiders}}</ref> in the [[Tamarin sector/Legends|Tamarin sector]].<ref name="TOR" />

==Behind the scenes==
The concept of ''akaan'gaan'' first appeared in the [[BioWare]]-made [[Star Wars video games|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]], ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', released [[December 20]], [[2011]]. To date, this has been the concept's only appearance.<ref name="TOR" />
